name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+23
Incumbent Rick Crawford running with a large financial advantage
Democrat Terri Green raised only $65k with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at 98%
model.rationale: Crawford is an incumbent in a deeply Republican northeast Arkansas district, out-raising Green more than 14-to-1 and holding over $1 million on hand. With no polls, no expert ratings moving the race, and markets at 98% Republican, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Crawford win.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a dramatic national Democratic wave environment would be needed to put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Crawford seeks another term in a district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan advantage of about 23 points. He enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised over $940,000 and holding more than $1 million on hand. Challenger Terri Green has raised only about $65,000 and has little cash available, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings target this race, and prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98% chance of winning. The combination of incumbency, district lean, and the fundraising gap makes this one of the safest Republican-held House seats on the map this cycle.
